**Submitted: deviation (T4C), preferred level.**

Repair made this round, and the reason for it:

- I removed the apposition "as the customer". Checking § 1.6 confirmed that **"CUSTOMER(S)" is a defined term in this Agreement meaning Corio's sublicensees** ("one or more customers of the Corio Services … who obtains a sublicense from Corio"). Calling Corio "the customer" in operative text would therefore have created a definitional conflict with a term used throughout the Agreement — a substantive intent defect, not just a pattern-match issue. The grant is now a clean, contiguous actor-verb statement: "Corio may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Commerce One …".
- The section number stays inline ("11.3 Termination for Convenience.") so it renders consistently with §§ 11.1–11.2 and matches the citation in the comment.

Operative § 11.3 carries all four preferred elements: Corio's convenience termination right; 30 days' prior written notice; Commerce One's pro-rata refund of prepaid fees for the post-termination period; and no Commerce One convenience termination during the initial five-year term or any renewal term.

Nothing else was altered — §§ 11.1 and 11.2 (including the breach, insolvency and Software-specification sentences) are retained verbatim, and no survival tail, expense, procedural, damages, "in whole or in part", or "notwithstanding" language was added. The fallback (60–90 days' notice, three-month fee cap) is offered only as a negotiating step in the comment. Validation returned `ok:true` with minimality clean. This is my final submission on T4C.
